items.title: Sandra Stalker obituary
items.summary: My mother, the educationist Sandra Stalker, who has died of cancer aged 78, was not an academic expert on Shakespeare, Byron, Eliot, Yeats or Dylan, but she understood them intimately. In a classroom or in casual conversation in a pub she could explain how great literature impacts civilised societies and our shared humanity. She was one of nature’s great teachers. From the early 1970s onwards Sandra taught at schools in Warwickshire, and around 1989 was appointed head of the Harris school, Rugby. A keen rugby enthusiast, she took particular pride in leading the school to the English Schools…

items.title: Lis Riveros
items.summary: Lis Riveros lsmr2 Thu, 20/08/2026 - 08:23 My doctoral research, supervised by Professor Helen McCarthy, examines the cultural, political, and business history of the English brewing industry since 1939. It explores the broader role of commercial actors in shaping social and cultural life, with particular attention to the relationship between business and the state. items.title: Eleanor Pickford
items.summary: Eleanor Pickford ep646 Mon, 10/08/2026 - 09:03 I am a PhD candidate working primarily on the history of political thought in the medieval period. My dissertation examines the themes of utopia and ideality through texts by authors including John of Salisbury, Christine de Pizan and Dante Alighieri. In light of the limited presence of the medieval period in scholarship on utopia, I am interested in how authors such as these conceived of the possibilities and limits of human agency and how these conceptions were expressed in their visions of political communities.
